query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding Mo to the CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy composition will enhance tribo-corrosion resistance at elevated temperatures compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy in the as-cast or annealed condition
generation.intervention: Introducing a controlled amount of Mo into the CoCrFeMnNi alloy (e.g., a few atomic percent)
generation.conditions: High-temperature sliding contact in a corrosive environment (e.g., aqueous or molten salt), with elevated temperature up to typical service conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Mo-rich surface film or oxide layer on the alloy
generation.mechanism: Mo doping promotes a more stable and protective passive film, reducing simultaneous wear and corrosion by improving oxide film adherence and retarding substrate oxidation
generation.predicted_outcome: Moderate improvement in wear resistance and reduced corrosion rate under tribo-corrosion conditions relative to the baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy without Mo
generation.baseline: CoCrFeMnNi alloy without Mo doping, which already possesses reasonable mechanical and corrosion properties but lower resistance to aggressive, high-temperature tribo-corrosion
generation.boundary: Effectiveness depends on the specific Mo content and operative temperature range; insufficient data on exact optimum doping level
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative gain in tribo-corrosion lifetime is not established by the evidence currently available; further testing is required

falsification_experiment.design: Compare multiple CoCrFeMnNi-based alloy samples with varying Mo content (e.g., 0%, 3%, 5%, 7%), subject them to tribo-corrosion tests at elevated temperature, and measure both wear volume and corrosion current density over time.
measurements: Mass loss and wear track depth to assess wear resistance
Potentiodynamic polarization to determine corrosion current density and passivation characteristics
Surface and cross-sectional microscopic analysis of the oxide layers
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-doped alloy exhibits no improvement in wear volume or corrosion resistance compared with the baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
